findings.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1`** — `{{#unless automatic}}` is evaluated inside the `group-member` item view, whose context is the individual `member` (a `User`), not the parent `Group`. `User` records have no `automatic` attribute, so this always resolves falsy and the "remove" (×) icon is shown on **every** member row, including members of automatic groups — exactly the case this PR is supposed to handle correctly. The backend still rejects the removal (422 in `add_members`/`remove_member`, `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:69,88`), but `Discourse.Group#removeMember` (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-49`) has no `.catch`, so the admin gets silent failure with no feedback. Fix: gate the remove link on the parent group's `automatic` flag (e.g. pass it into the item view, or check `controller.automatic`/a bound property), and add error handling to `removeMember`.

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:21`** — `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. Ember's `{{each}}` "item form" in this era exposes item-view wiring via `itemViewClass`, not `itemView`; using an unrecognized hash option is likely to silently no-op, meaning the member list may not render at all via the custom item view. This should be manually verified by loading the admin group page; if confirmed, rename to `itemViewClass="group-member"`.

**`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90`** — `group.users.delete(user_id)` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if `user_id` doesn't belong to the group's current membership (e.g., double-click, stale UI, already-removed member) — Rails resolves bare ids via `find` before deleting. There's no rescue, so this becomes an unhandled 500 for what should be a benign/idempotent operation. Wrap in a rescue (or check membership first) and return a normal success/404 instead of blowing up.

**Test coverage gap** — There is no spec at all for `GroupsController#members` (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`), even though this PR's core fix (removing the automatic-group-only pagination limitation, returning the new `{members, meta}` shape) lives there. This is the most behaviorally significant change in the diff and ships with zero test coverage.

**`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115`** — `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` uses the `PUT` verb, but `config/routes.rb:49` maps `remove_member` to `DELETE` only (the later, correct test at line 125 uses `:delete`). This is an internal inconsistency in the test suite; even if `ActionController::TestCase` is lenient about verb/route matching, it should be `:delete` for correctness and to guard against future routing constraints tightening.

**`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-96`** — `add_members`/`remove_member` call `group.save` after the membership mutation already happened via `group.add`/`group.users.delete` (both of which persist immediately). If `group.save` fails for unrelated reasons, the response reports an error even though the membership change already took effect — misleading success/failure semantics. Consider dropping the redundant `save` or reloading/checking membership state directly.

**`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71`** — `usernames.split(",")` doesn't strip whitespace; `"bob, alice"` yields `" alice"`, which will silently fail to match any user via `find_by_username`. Trim each entry before lookup.
**`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22`** — no upper bound on `params[:limit]`; a client can request an arbitrarily large page size. Consider clamping (e.g. `[limit, 200].min`).

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65`** — `addMembers` action has a `// TODO: should clear the input` and no `.catch` on the resulting promise, so failed adds (e.g., duplicate/invalid usernames) are silent.

API response shape change for `/groups/:group_id/members.json` (array → `{members, meta}`) is a breaking change for any external/API consumers of that endpoint; worth a changelog/doc note even though all in-repo callers were updated consistently.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `group-member` view (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) and uses it via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. In the Ember/Handlebars style used by Discourse in this era, `itemView` is a recognized option on `{{each}}` (commonly used in Discourse templates to render an array via a named item view). Therefore, this is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff, and there’s no concrete evidence here that `itemView` would silently no-op or prevent rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90`** — `group.users.delete(user_id)` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if `user_id` doesn't belong to the group's current membership (e.g., double-click, stale UI, already-removed member) — Rails resolves bare ids via `find` before deleting. There's no rescue, so this becomes an unhandled 500 for what should be a benign/idempotent operation. Wrap in a rescue (or check membership first) and return a normal success/404 instead of blowing up.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` comes directly from params. In Rails, `collection_association.delete(id)` resolves ids by doing a scoped `find` on the association before removing, which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the id is not present in the association (e.g., user already removed / stale UI) or even if the user id doesn’t exist. There is no rescue/handling here, so this can surface as an unhandled 500 for what should be an idempotent/remove operation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes a significant behavioral/API change to `GroupsController#members` (always paginates, changes response shape to `{ members, meta }`, new defaults), but the only spec file modified in the diff is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`. There are no added/updated specs shown for `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`. However, the finding’s absolute claim that there is “no spec at all” / “zero test coverage” for `GroupsController#members` cannot be verified from this diff alone (tests could exist elsewhere and be unchanged). What is verifiable is that this PR does not add/update tests for that changed action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-96`** — `add_members`/`remove_member` call `group.save` after the membership mutation already happened via `group.add`/`group.users.delete` (both of which persist immediately). If `group.save` fails for unrelated reasons, the response reports an error even though the membership change already took effect — misleading success/failure semantics. Consider dropping the redundant `save` or reloading/checking membership state directly.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` mutates membership inside the loop via `group.add(user)`, and `#remove_member` mutates membership via `group.users.delete(user_id)`. Both of these are association-level operations that typically hit the join table immediately (they are not staged in the `Group` object waiting for `group.save`). Immediately after, both actions conditionally render success/error based on `if group.save`. Since `group.save` is saving the `Group` record (which wasn’t modified here) and can fail due to unrelated validations/callbacks, it can report an error even though the membership change has already been applied, producing misleading semantics. This mismatch is directly observable from the controller code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71`** — `usernames.split(",")` doesn't strip whitespace; `"bob, alice"` yields `" alice"`, which will silently fail to match any user via `find_by_username`. Trim each entry before lookup.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then calls `User.find_by_username(username)` without stripping whitespace. If the client submits a comma-separated list with spaces (e.g. "bob, alice"), the second token will be " alice" and will not match an existing username, causing the add to silently skip that user. This is a concrete correctness issue visible in the diff and is not handled elsewhere in this method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22`** — no upper bound on `params[:limit]`; a client can request an arbitrarily large page size. Consider clamping (e.g. `[limit, 200].min`).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)`. There is no clamp/maximum enforced on `params[:limit]`, so a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, potentially causing very large DB queries and response payloads (performance/DoS risk). This behavior is clearly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65`** — `addMembers` action has a `// TODO: should clear the input` and no `.catch` on the resulting promise, so failed adds (e.g., duplicate/invalid usernames) are silent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `addMembers` calling `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without returning the promise or attaching a `.catch`, and it includes a TODO about clearing the input. However, the claim that failures are "silent" is not verifiable from this diff alone: `Discourse.ajax(...)` may already provide global error handling/user feedback, and nothing in the diff demonstrates that duplicate/invalid usernames produce an unhandled, user-invisible failure. The TODO is an acknowledged enhancement, not a defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: API response shape change for `/groups/:group_id/members.json` (array → `{members, meta}`) is a breaking change for any external/API consumers of that endpoint; worth a changelog/doc note even though all in-repo callers were updated consistently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns a plain serialized list/array response) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e., an object with `members` and `meta` keys. That is an API response shape change for `/groups/:group_id/members(.json)` and would break any external clients expecting the previous array payload, even though in-repo JS callers were updated to read `result.members`/`result.meta`.
